questions.title: Who will score India's first half-century in the July 2026 Twenty20 international series against Zimbabwe?
questions.background: A half-century in cricket is an individual score of at least 50 runs in one innings.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the first Indian batter to reach 50 runs in an innings during the July 2026 men's Twenty20 international series against Zimbabwe, according to official match scorecards and contemporaneous match reports. Resolution Date : 2026-07-23 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the batter's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Updating for three India T20Is played since June 24 (Ireland 1st/2nd T20I and England 1st T20I on July 1), even though the Harare squad (July 23-26) won't be named until mid-July. Explosive T20I-only opener Abhishek Sharma moves clearly into #1 (0.16 -> 0.19) after blasting 59 off 24 balls in Durham on July 1 (fastest ever to 100 T20I sixes) on top of 49 in Belfast; he finishes the England T20Is on July 11 (12 days before Harare), is not in the ODI XI, previously hit a T20I ton in Harare (2024), and reaches 50 faster than any opening partner. Conversely, 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi trims slightly (0.16 -> 0.14) after being left out of India's XI for three straight T20Is (both Ireland games and England opener) with team management reiterating he must wait his turn—still a strong Zimbabwe-tour debut candidate, but less guaranteed to open Match 1 and unproven at international level. Sanju Samson trims from 0.13 to 0.11 after three consecutive low scores (including a 1 in Durham that intensified calls for Sooryavanshi). T20I vice-captain Tilak Varma holds at 0.14 (prime #3/captaincy candidate if ODI regulars Shreyas Iyer and new ICC World No. 1 T20I batter Ishan Kishan are rested after England ODIs end July 19), with Yashasvi Jaiswal steady at 0.08 and 34.0% on the field (Ishan Kishan, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Shreyas Iyer, Shivam Dube, Riyan Parag).

questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: WHO's June 19, 2026 Disease Outbreak News (DON608) reports 896 confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases (over 1,000 by June 24) across Ituri (817 cases, 91.1%, 21/36 health zones), North Kivu (~60+ cases, 11/35 health zones), and South Kivu (1/34 health zones), with no licensed Bundibugyo vaccine available. While Ituri remains the conflict-ridden epicenter with 4,659 contacts and ongoing expansion into new health zones, North Kivu is accelerating rapidly—jumping from 7 to 11 affected health zones and 699 to 1,628 contacts in 11 days, with Goma already impacted and high displacement—making Ituri and North Kivu near-even co-favorites for a mid-September weekly surge. South Kivu (already affected and linked to Goma across Lake Kivu) is the main tertiary risk, with adjacent provinces Tshopo and Haut-Uele holding smaller spillover probabilities.

local_articles.title: Ebola death toll in DR Congo surpasses 500
local_articles.snippet: eadliest outbreak in the DR Congo resulted in nearly 2,300 deaths out of 3,500 recorded cases between 2018 and 2020. The 17th epidemic in the DR Congo, officially declared on May 15, is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which there is neither a vaccine nor a treatment. A clinical trial involving two treatments for this rare strain began on Thursday, according to the WHO, which also granted emergency use authorisation for the first molecular diagnostic test for the virus. Officials have yet to identify the outbreak’s patient zero and still need to trace possibly tens of thousands of people who have come in contact with infected individuals. The first month of this Ebola outbreak was already the worst on record, the WHO has said. questions.title: Whom will Donald Trump endorse in the 2026 Republican primary for Tennessee's Ninth Congressional District?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : as established by Trump's public statements or contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution Date : ahead of the August 6, 2026 primary. Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the candidate's first and last name.
questions.current_reasoning: Following Tennessee's Trump-backed May 7, 2026 mid-decade redistricting of TN-09 after Louisiana v. Callais, exactly four Republicans qualified for the August 6 primary: State Sen. Brent Taylor, State Rep. Todd Warner, Charlotte Bergmann, and Jeremy Thompson. Taylor launched minutes after the map passed, immediately self-funded $1 million, and locked up endorsements from both U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn and Bill Hagerty (who called him 'exactly who President Trump needs'), House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, and 50+ Tennessee GOP officials. Trump routinely aligns with leadership and clear frontrunners in newly drawn GOP seats ahead of early voting (July 17), making Brent Taylor an overwhelming favorite over Warner and Bergmann.

questions.title: Which NBA team will LeBron James choose for the 2026–27 season?
questions.background: This question concerns James's publicly announced team choice for the upcoming NBA season.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : James's public announcement of his team choice for the 2026–27 season during the 2026 offseason, corroborated by reputable news or sports reporting. Resolution Date : Resolve when James publicly announces that choice. A completed contract signing or appearance in a game is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The full name of the NBA team he chooses.
questions.current_reasoning: Late July 3 and July 4 reporting (HoopsHype citing Shams Charania at 11:58 PM ET, Sports Review News citing updated Kalshi pricing, NBC Sports, SI/Yossi Gozlan, Ballislife/DraftKings) drives a sharp repricing between Philadelphia and Golden State. First, Shams Charania formally narrowed LeBron James's decision to six teams: Cavaliers, Heat, Nuggets, Sixers, Timberwolves, and Warriors, while reiterating the choice 'will not be a financially driven money decision'—undercutting Golden State's $15M NTMLE edge. Second, Kalshi repriced sharply by July 3 close (reported July 4): Cleveland 46%, Philadelphia surging to 19% (overtaking GSW!), Golden State sliding 10 points to 17%, Miami 10%, and all others <=4%, while earlier-July-3 DraftKings odds (-115 Cavs, +180 Warriors, +900 Heat, +1000 Sixers, +1200 Nuggets) lagged the podcast fallout. Third, cap analyst Yossi Gozlan revealed Philadelphia has a pathway to offer $6.7M (Dean Wade sign-and-trade plus swapping two non-guaranteed deals)—potentially the largest salary among Rich Paul's five inner-circle teams—while NBC Sports highlighted that Golden State looked like the long shot on Paul's whiteboard and Denver remains stalled on Peyton Watson's RFA. Blending updated Kalshi, DraftKings, and reporting: Cleveland edges up to 0.45 (+0.01), Golden State drops to 0.19 (-0.05), Philadelphia jumps to 0.16 (+0.06), Miami trims to 0.11 (-0.02), and Denver holds 0.045, leaving 4.5% mainly for Minnesota (~3.5%) and any surprise outside the final six.

local_articles.title: Glasner joins Forest after silverware-filled spell at Palace
local_articles.snippet: July 6 - Oliver Glasner has been appointed head coach of Nottingham Forest, the Premier League club said on Monday, succeeding Vítor Pereira and a string of managers before him over the last year. Fifty-one-year-old Glasner became a free agent at the end of a successful spell at Crystal Palace that included an FA Cup triumph and a UEFA Conference League title. Over the past year Forest have churned through managers at a remarkable pace: Nuno Espírito Santo was sacked in September 2025, Ange Postecoglou lasted 39 days before being dismissed in October, Sean Dyche was fired in February after 114 days, and then Pereira took over, making Forest the first Premier League club to have four different permanent managers in a single season. questions.title: Which U.S. state will be the first to impose a statewide moratorium on construction of large new hyperscale data centres?
questions.background: Hyperscale data centres are large facilities designed to provide computing and storage capacity at massive scale. Their development can place substantial demands on electricity grids and water supplies.
questions.resolution_criteria: Qualifying Event : Resolve to the first U.S. state to formally impose, by December 31, 2026, a statewide temporary moratorium on construction or permitting of large new hyperscale data centres. Proposed legislation, vetoed measures, and restrictions limited to individual municipalities do not qualify. Source of Truth : Official state-government announcements, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution occurs when the qualifying moratorium is publicly announced as imposed. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the state.
questions.current_reasoning: According to the Rockefeller Institute's June 10, 2026 tracker of 14 states weighing data center moratoria, Maine's bill was vetoed by Gov. Janet Mills on April 24 (override failed April 29), leaving New York as the ONLY state whose legislature has passed a statewide moratorium (a compromise 1-year freeze on >=20 MW facilities passed both chambers June 4). Gov. Kathy Hochul faces re-election in November 2026 amid intense utility-bill pushback and signaled openness ('the status quo can't continue'), giving New York a commanding lead (including potential signing with chapter amendments). If Hochul vetoes, full-time legislatures still in session (Michigan, Pennsylvania) or states with prior momentum or executive options (Maine, Virginia, plus ~11% across California, New Jersey, Massachusetts, and others) remain secondary contenders.

local_articles.title: Lawsuit filed against Eagan asks court to void city's data center moratorium
local_articles.snippet: A lawsuit filed against the City of Eagan is asking a Minnesota court to void the Twin Cities suburb's data center moratorium. The complaint, filed on behalf of the Minnesota company Eagan Capital, LLC, on June 15, claims the city is "seeking to regulate energy usage" through the moratorium, which it called "ill-advised" and "unlawful." The interim ordinance passed unanimously by the Eagan City Council on Feb. 17 states that "no new data center may be located in Eagan within 500 feet of residential homes or use more than 20 megawatts of electricity through Feb. 17, 2027, unless the Council lifts the moratorium earlier," the city's website said. According to the complaint, which cited Minnesota law, the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission regulates the electricity industry in Minnesota, including electricity demand, and the City of Eagan doesn't have the authority to do so.
